newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Jurong Shipyard holds S$220 mln shipbuilding jobs.
newsitem.headline: Jurong Shipyard holds S$220 mln shipbuilding jobs.

text.p: Jurong Shipyard Ltd's 1997 revenue from repairing and upgrading off-shore floating structures is expected to be Singapore $100 million, company officials said on Saturday.
The shiprepair group said it was building seven vessels worth a total of S$220 million.
Managing director Tan Kwi Kin said jobs from repairing and upgrading the floating structures would bring in S$100 million this year for the group.
"We already got quite a number of ships from this business. It will roll in S$100 million in revenue for 1997. That would cushion the depressed ship repair business," Tan said.

The work in hand, including three checkup jobs, are valued at S$40 million. Tan said Jurong planned to achieve S$50 million in revenue in the six months to June this year and that it was looking to tender for more jobs.

But he said ship repair would remain Jurong's core business. "By the end of 1997, ship repair will contribute about 70 percent of our total revenue. The rest will be from building and conversion," Tan said.
"We will be happy if we achieve a long-term target of 60 percent contribution from repairs, 20 percent from building and 20 percent from conversion," he added.
Tan said said shipbuilding in 1997 was expected to be "very busy", with the docks fully occupied till May.
Of the seven vessels it is building, two are scheduled to be delivered in the second half of 1997 and the rest in 1998-1999.
In 1995, the company had no contribution from this sector. Its dock expansion last year allowed it to accept bigger jobs from Ultra-Large Capacity Carriers and Very Large Capacity Carriers.

"With the added capacity from our new docks, we have the intention to capture some of the off-shore floating structure jobs like check-ups. In five to 10 years, many of these structures would be due for repairs and upgrading," Tan said.
So far, customers are from the United States, Vietnam, India and Asia, Tan said.
The building jobs comprised four container ships, one product carrier, a bulk carrier and achemical carrier.
